utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning to you all. Would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we begin our today's business, there's a matter in the course of yesterday's hearing that need to be clarified. Yesterday, when Mr. Nicholls's question, whether the witness was truthful when making his statement to the Prosecution was objected to by the Defence, the Chamber allowed the question to be put to the witness by a majority, with me dissenting. However, I feel obliged to comment that it was a mistake on my part, and I would like to make it clear now that the Chamber cannot make a decision if the opinions are split between Judge Prost and me when sitting pursuant to 15 bis in the absence of Judge Agius. Unfortunately, what happened happened, however I don't think that raised a serious problem in the overall conduct of the trial. Having said that -- I forgot to mention that today we sit pursuant to 15 bis. Now we turn to the issue which is before us. We have carefully reviewed the submission made by the parties yesterday on the issues before us. Let me first deal with two submissions advanced by Mr. Bourgon, with regard to the conduct of the Prosecution. In short, we do not find merit in these arguments. As to the questioning of a witness regarding what the other party has discussed with him or her, we see no reason why that is inappropriate or unethical. No authorities in support of the proposition were provided, and it would seem to be a practice entirely consistent with the concept that there is no property in the witness, a principle which both parties agreed upon. As to allegations that the witness was pressured by the Prosecution, there is nothing in the description of the meeting provided, or the information sheet that evidences any such pressure. In these particular circumstances, reminding a witness of the need to need to tell the truth when testifying cannot be construed as threatening or pressuring him. We turn now to the most significant issue, which arises from a question posed by Mr. Nicholls and objected to by the Defence. When Mr. Nicholls seeks to adduce -- Mr. Nicholls seeks to adduce evidence as to what the witness told him about seeing Drago Nikolic at the check-point on the day in question, we have carefully reviewed the transcript of the witness's evidence yesterday, in particular the two passages referenced by Mr. Bourgon. That is, page 64, lines 11 to 17; and page 66, lines 14 to 22. We have also had regard to paragraph 10 of his previous statement. We have come to the conclusion that both his testimony and his prior statement are open to varying interpretation on the essential question. While this Trial Chamber rarely intervenes in the questioning process, in this particular instance, however, we have decided that it would be appropriate for us to do so. Both parties have made reference to possible fears that the witness might have and pressure which he might be feeling. A good portion of the submission presented have centred on meetings held by counsel for the Prosecution and counsel for the Defence with the witness. In these special circumstances, we believe that it would be in the interest of justice for the Chamber itself to clarify the issue with the witness. Therefore, the witness can be brought into the courtroom at this time, and Judge Prost will question him on behalf of the Chamber on this one issue. Draw the curtain and please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I have to apologise to you again for the delay in your testimony. As happens from time to time, we have been discussing some procedural and legal questions relating to your testimony. We have decided there is a part of your evidence which is not clear to us, and so in this instance the Chamber is going to try and clarify the matter with you. To that end, my learned colleague, Judge Prost, is now going to ask you some questions. But please bear in mind that you are still under the solemn declaration you took yesterday. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you were telling us about what happened while you were at the check-point near the school in Rocevic. What is not clear to us is whether you yourself saw Drago Nikolic at this check-point. So my specific question to you is, while you were at the check-point that day, at any time, when these security officers arrived, while they were parked there, or when they left, did you yourself actually see Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally did not see Drago Nikolic. I saw another security officer though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: And which other security officer did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday, Witness, you said that you recalled having a meeting with Mr. Nicholls from the office of the Prosecution last week and talking to him about this part of the statement. Do you remember that meeting with Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: And at that time, in that meeting with Mr. Nicholls, did you tell him that you, in fact, had seen Drago Nikolic at the check-point that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that when the vehicle went past, Trbic came out and that there were other security officers there with him. And what they told us, the orders they conveyed to us, we discussed this, me and my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, I think that's the farthest we can reach, and I leave it in your hands. Now it's your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where exactly was it that you saw Trbic? At the check-point or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across from the check-point in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: School-yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And there was one colleague working the check-point with you. Is that I think what you said yesterday. I just want to be clear on that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And is it that colleague or somebody else who told you that Drago Nikolic had come through and was with Trbic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That colleague said security officer Trbic and Drago Nikolic, but I saw Trbic but I didn't see Nikolic. But that's what we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to move on. I'm going to ask you, you said yesterday you stayed there until about 5.00 p.m. I just want you to think about that. Is that right or could it have been earlier or later that you left the check-point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, thereabouts, 1700 hours, because afterwards I went to the hospital and at around 1830 hours I was already at the brigade headquarters. That's the amount of time I needed to get to the hospital and back to the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And very briefly, without mentioning any names, tell us why you went to the hospital, just so that the Chamber knows.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my wife was there. She was nine months pregnant, and she went for a medical check-up before giving birth, and I escorted her and then went to the centre of town where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And when you say you went to the headquarters, just for clarity, that's Zvornik Brigade headquarters, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I reported to the commander to tell him that I had arrived, and in the premises I found the company. I said that I had arrived, and I came across several of the staff from our company and two colleagues from the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you see any security officers at Standard, at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that evening, when I arrived, when I arrived to the premises of our company, up the stairs there were a few people walking around, and they were wearing camouflage uniforms and I saw their backs and I asked who that was and one of them said, "Well, the commander has a meeting with Popovic and Beara."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at that time did you know who Popovic was? Think carefully.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I personally did not know who Popovic was. And I told you that the first time as well. But from the back and the front I saw that he had a moustache, and after 1998, when I said on those panorama things that I saw that it was that same Popovic person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What is this Popovic person's first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Vujadin Popovic. That's what I remember the name down there from the warrant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was Vujadin Popovic's position in July 1995? You know, what was his job, put it that way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew and I heard that this man Popovic was a security officer of the -- could the Court --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the name of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking you if you could repeat the name of the corps that Vujadin Popovic was a security officer in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Drina Corps, to which the Zvornik Brigade belonged as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, when you were an MP in the Zvornik Brigade in July 1995, and you've told us about how you had duties at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters, did you know in July 1995 that Vujadin Popovic was a security officer for the corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. How do you mean security officer for the corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You've told us that Vujadin Popovic, you said, "I heard that this man Popovic was a security officer," and then you said for the Drina Corps. When did you know that? Did you know that in July 1995 when you had been an MP for a year and a half?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly. I knew it a little before that, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Little before when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three months, perhaps, earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Earlier than July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you know Vujadin Popovic by sight in July 1995? I'm not asking if you played cards with him, if you visited his house. I'm asking if, you know, if he came through the gate at Standard, did you recognise him and know who this was, or would you have checked his ID and, you know, searched him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably if he were to pass by me and I were at the gate or at the hut at the gate, well, I didn't know him, nor did I know him close up, so I probably would have checked to see whether that was the man Popovic and then I would personally know that it was or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you saw -- when you were at the brigade headquarters that night, we're talking about -- and you talked about hearing that this security officer Popovic was there, were you able to see -- you said you saw his moustache. Did you see clearly Vujadin Popovic at the brigade that night? And please try to think carefully about this and answer carefully. And if you need help remembering, again, if you think it will help you, I can show you your statement where you talk about this. Statements, I should say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that point in time, when I was in the hallway, up the stairs, upstairs, from the left as he was walking up the stairs, I saw that side of his face, from the left side, and I saw the moustache. He was a tall man wearing a camouflage uniform. Whether it was an overall or in two parts, I can't say, but that's what I saw with the moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And you said he was with somebody named Beara. Did you know this person Beara at that time, in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Nor did I ever see him. He was never close to me. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what were you told, you started to tell us, that Vujadin Popovic and this person who you were told was Beara were doing at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters that night up the stairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, my colleague said they had a meeting with the commander. So we were talking about this and made some noise. And the commander said, "What do you need to know who's up there, none of your business." So he stopped us talking and we quietened down. And the commander at that time was Obrenovic. He was performing the duties of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Which commander was he, when you said the commander said, "Quiet down"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the military police company. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Miomir Jasikovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So this is the same day that you are performing duties at the Rocevic School, you've said it's the only day you ever performed duties at the Rocevic School, it's the same night, that's the night we're talking about that Popovic and Beara are meeting with the commander and you're told to be quiet. Is that right, just for clarity, all the same day here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question, Mr. President, because he had clearly said he was told about Beara. The question seems to imply that he may have seen him when he did not. He clearly testified that he was just told that, never saw him before. So I think the question is not properly placed. And I object as to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That can be rephrased, Mr. Nicholls. Without affecting the content of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just to be very clear, this meeting that you've heard about is on -- we're all talking about one day here, correct, it's the same day, the same night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And as far as you were told, just to be clear, because of the objection, Vujadin Popovic and this person who you were told Beara, you said, were there to meet with who? Who were they meeting with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my colleagues said that they had a meeting with the commander. And during that time the acting commander was Colonel Obrenovic, or Lieutenant-Colonel Obrenovic, while the main commander was absent. So that's probably it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So your understanding was the meeting was with the commander of the Zvornik Brigade at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of the Zvornik Brigade that was replacing Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Mr. Zivanovic, you will begin your cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Witness, can you confirm that you met me on two occasions as well as with members of my team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you go further, I would like to let you know that Mr. Zivanovic is representing Mr. Popovic. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, you do recall that on that occasion I told you, and put it to you, that -- what you said in your statement given in the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Among other things, do you remember -- do you remember me -- telling me about the contents of your statement with regard to Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on that occasion you told me that at the time of making the statement you didn't tell the Tribunal investigators that you knew Vujadin Popovic at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that at that time I didn't know him personally but that I got to know him from the panorama and from the warrant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember telling me on that occasion that you never saw Vujadin Popovic in Zvornik but you only heard that he had a meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that they had a meeting and that they went upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let me be quite clear. You said that on that occasion you didn't see Vujadin Popovic at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the whole figure, but I saw him from the left side on the stairs, and then in 1998, 1999, I remember that that was the person in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But when you talked to me, you didn't even tell me that you saw him in part. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we discussed the hall and the stairs, and I said that I saw his left side, and that I didn't see this other person. I think that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know, and fortunately I wasn't alone, I remember you saying that you didn't see him at all, but things do change and probably your memory has changed. Tell me one more thing now. You gave your statement in 2005, which means 10 years after all the events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is only natural for a person to match their memories or to split it into several days. Tell me, as much as you can remember that particular day that you gave your testimony about, how well do you remember all these details, and how reliable is your recollection of this one single day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to try and say, but I must say that 75 per cent of my memory is not serving me well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Upon your arrival in The Hague, you had an interview with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I noticed inter alia that you had been asked about an event which took place in 1992. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just asked about this by Mr. Prosecutor, and I don't think there is any need for us to discuss it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just want to ask my colleague, I see that there is a witness statement on his exhibit list, if he's going to show that or go into it. I think because of the nature of it, it should be in private session and if we need to talk about why, we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But I think my friend may agree that it's, because of the sake of the declarant of that witness statement, it would be better not to use the name or go into it in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not going to use the report submitted to us. I only mentioned it in another context that I'm going to question the witness about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that same occasion, when you were asked about this statement and when a statement given by a Muslim person was shown to you, did you also discuss this event on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which event are you referring to, the one from 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just want to be clear, this may help my friend, if it wasn't clear in his statement. He was not shown any witness statement of anybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber was not able to follow either. Shall we go into private session and show the witness the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He's never seen the statement. That's just what I was trying to clarify, and I don't think necessarily that he needs to. I think my friend was going to ask him questions about the event without showing it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day that you mentioned, you received an order to go to the school in Rocevici and to carry out the duties that you have been describing. Can you please tell me, in your statement you said that you left the check-point at around 1800 hours. Here you said 1700 hours. Is the time that you mentioned in the statement correct, or is it the one that you said today correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said in my statement that it was around 1700 hours because it was impossible for me to reach Zvornik -- or headquarters from Zvornik in such a short lapse of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now take a look at your statement, that's 3D97, item 11. That's on page 3. 0465-3512. Can you please read item 11 where you say, "At 1800 hours I left the check-point and went to the hospital in Zvornik," and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you can see that you said, "At 1800 hours." Was your memory more fresh at the time, or today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 1730 or 1800, it makes no difference. There is a long distance to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the question was when you left the check-point, not how many kilometres there were and how many -- how much time it took.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I may have said 1800 hours or 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me now how you left the check-point? Did you have your own car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hitchhiked from the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I left on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask anybody's permission to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police commander, Miomir Jasikovac, when he gave me an order on that day, I told him that I had to go to the hospital in the evening. He said, "Go there and be there until 1800 hours and then go to the hospital and after that report to the HQ," and that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that occasion when, as you said, you had seen Popovic at the brigade HQ, you mentioned another four persons being there. You can take a look at item 3 [as interpreted], where their names are listed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I had an opportunity to read the statements given by these individuals, and not a single one of them has confirmed this part of your statement that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone is responsible for their statements. I have no knowledge about their statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, everybody makes their own statements, and everybody has their own memory.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So item 3 should read "item 13." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly ask this to be rectified. I referred the witness to item 13, not 3. But I think he did understand me, that he looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I've seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were looking at paragraph 13, it was mistranslated as paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no objection. I think my friend just needs to wait a minute before he asks his next question. Because as I can hear it, he's asking questions as soon as the witness finishes and the translation may not be as accurate as it could be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for your intervention. I have nothing to do then. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you one more thing. You said in your first statement that you knew Vujadin Popovic very well. If you wish you may take a look. It's item 12 of your statement where you say that you had seen security officer Vujadin Popovic, who you knew very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed this, and with Mr. Nicholls, the Prosecutor, I considered this matter that has been noted down as such, but I knew him only after 1998 and 1999, after I recognised him from the warrant. And I realised that that was the person from the year 1995, and I think that Mr. Nicholls acknowledged that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, only after you had seen the warrant you remembered that it might have been the person you saw in 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I discussed that with the gentleman in question, and we considered this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Who will be the next?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I leave it in the hands of Defence counsel, but I take it that we can finish the cross-examination by today?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It seems that we would be able to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. Sir you mentioned on your direct examination that a colleague told you about this purported meeting upstairs in the Zvornik Brigade. Can you tell me which colleague or colleagues told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the military police colleagues. I know they were there. The administrative staff was there. But they didn't talk about that. It was the colleagues, the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What I would like to know, sir, is which colleague or colleagues told you this information that you claim to have remembered 10 or so years after the events that upstairs there were some security officers in the Zvornik Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the colleagues because one person would be there one day and wouldn't be there the next. They kept changing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on page 12, line 11 of today's transcript when you were asked by my learned friend about Mr. Popovic, you also added that you did not see this other person. Is that correct, sir? And the other person we're referencing is the claim that your colleague told you that possibly Mr. Beara was there, correct? Is that who the other person is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think that reflects what the witness said. He is now reading back to him the -- as what he said. The -- what the witness said, to my recollection, was that he was told that this other person was Beara, not this -- there was no "possible" thrown into the witness's answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but shall we look at...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 12, line 11 I was referencing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "I said that I saw his left side and that I didn't see this other person."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I'm clarifying who he was referencing when he said he didn't see this other person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The way he phrased his question was, "When you were told by your colleague that there was this possible Beara," and when the witness answered the question at line 6, 20, he said, "Well the commander has a meeting with Popovic and Beara." That was his answer about who the meeting was with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ostojic is trying to clarify who that person was that he didn't see at that time when he saw Mr. Popovic climbing up the stairs. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The person -- if I could just put the question to him again, if I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The person that you mentioned that you did not see, the other person on page 12, line 11, that was the person that you were told by someone else, whose name you don't know, that that was purportedly Mr. Beara, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you -- could you read that part again to the witness, although witness already confirmed that --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Twice now, but I will. The question and the answer, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Would you do that, please. Read the transcript correctly and then confirm with the witness again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness I'm just trying to clarify. I know you've given us an answer and I apologise for that. On page 12 of today's transcript you were asked by my learned friend from the Prosecutor starting on line 8, he states, "But when you talked to me you didn't even tell me that you saw him in part; is that correct?" Your answer, sir, which commences on line 10 was, "Yes, we discussed the hall and the stairs and I said that I saw his left side and that I didn't see this other person. I think that's what I said." Focusing on your answer that you gave on line 11 of page 12, "that I didn't see this other person," that other person is supposed to be, at least according to the Prosecutor, what you were told by some unknown person to be Mr. Beara, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you now mentioned that I talked to you. As I understand it, I didn't talk to you except now. You are just asking me something now. Now, this colleague conveyed to me that up the stairs was Popovic and Beara, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you never saw this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For clarification, that question was put, in my memory, by Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, and just do clarify that, you never met with me or any of the Beara Defence team members, correct, at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Also, sir, on page 9, lines 4 through 5, you state that you never saw -- let me just get the cite for you here. You state that you never saw him before, and the person you're referencing there is Mr. Beara, correct? You never saw him before, during that purported visit, or after that visit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I never saw him, neither before nor afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Nor during that purported meeting at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I just want to clarify it, sir. Thank you. Let me ask you this just for the record so that it's clear. How many meetings did you have with the Office of the Prosecutor? And I have them written down here as your first meeting was March -- or November 26, 2005, it was an interview which you signed that interview. Then you had one March 22, 2007, which was a short meeting and you signed that interview. And then according to the information that we have from the Prosecutor, you met him on two occasions after that, or more, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first time was (redacted) (redacted) and I had the chance of meeting him. And the other statement I gave through my Ministry of Defence, two of them. Once I met with the Prosecutor here in preparing, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just to be cautious, could we have a redaction of lines -- the second sentence starting at 23/16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are considering that matter. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So I am only focusing on the interviews or the meetings that you had with the Office of the Prosecutor and Mr. Nicholls, my learned friend, regarding your testimony here. I have it that in the last two weeks or so you met him on three occasions: March 22nd, March 23rd, and the 29th of March, 2007. Is that accurate or did you meet him more than on those three occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I met him up there two or three times. I've been a long -- many days so I don't quite remember. But we didn't discuss these topics here. It was just the first day that we discussed these topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that would have been March 22nd, 2007. I'm just curious to know why the Prosecutor, if you know, Witness, would have, on the 22nd, have you sign a statement but if there were any other changes or modifications to your statement, given your testimony here yesterday and today, on the 23rd or the 29th, why didn't they have you sign another statement? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I object to that. There is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Whether -- it is for the witness to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. There is no way he could know what was in my mind and why I make -- I don't always know why I make the decisions I make. There's no way he can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, could you rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you at any time given that the 22nd of March, 2007 you signed this supplemental or interview statement, did you at any time on the 23rd of March, 2007, refuse to sign a supplemental information sheet or additional data that Mr. Nicholls and you may have talked about on that day? Did you refuse to sign that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that I needed to sign anything on that day. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the same answer would hold true for the 29th of March, 2007, correct, sir, when you met with the Prosecutor and you gave us another what they call information report, you weren't asked to sign that, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think I signed anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You haven't, from our information. And you didn't refuse to sign anything, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He's answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's in reference to specifically the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On this, yes. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you didn't refuse to sign anything on the 29th of March, 2007, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't really remember that I signed anything. Really, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's fair, sir. Let me ask you one other question on this point on your meetings with the Office of the Prosecutor that you may have had. At any time did you refuse them, if they made such a request, to tape record the meetings or interviews that they may have had with you on the 23rd of March or the 29th of March of this year? Did they ever offer to tape record so that we could get the sum and substance of what happens at those meetings? Did they ever offer to tape record their meetings with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody ever offered me anything, offered to tape anything or record anything or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you share with us, when you told us on page 12, that 75 per cent of your memory is not serving well, can you expand on that, please? And I believe it commences on lines 19 through 23. But also 24 and 25, according to my notes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that 75 to 80 per cent of my memory does serve me, still serves me, not that it does not serve me. That my memory serves me to the extent of between 75 and 80 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it serves you, sir, with respect to the events that happened 12 years ago, you remember this specific one incident. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's all the questions I have. Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you today which relates to your testimony when you were asked to go to the Sepak border crossing. My first question to you is simply that this border crossing in Sepak, in terms of its location, would I be right in saying that this was on the northern side of Rocevic School, approximately eight to 10 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Rocevic down the Drina River about eight to 10 kilometres towards Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, if I can have the exhibit which was used by the Prosecution yesterday, and that was P2494. Oh, but the one that was marked by the witness is better, and I'm given another number here, which would be 0083. IC, IC00-0083, marked map. If we could have this on e-court, please. Now, Witness, I'm just going to ask you to look at this map which will appear in front of you, and simply if you can indicate where this Sepak border crossing is, if you can see it on that map. While we wait for this I'll go to my next question to try and save some time. The phone call that you received that day, you were personally on the phone with Jasikovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would I be right to say that Jasikovac at that time was in the Zvornik Brigade command, and that is in the Standard. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where it was. He had to call me from somewhere. It needn't have been from the Standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So it could have been in another location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, the map is before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, now we now have the map on the e-court, and yesterday you indicated with an arrow pointing one side with a Z towards Zvornik and one side with a B towards Bijeljina. Can you indicate first on which side towards Bijeljina is the Sepak border crossing and if you can indicate on this map, the furthest you can, in which direction is the Sepak border crossing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Usher will assist you in marking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can't see Sepak on the map here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I understand, Witness, that it cannot be seen here, but the furthest away from -- on the map, the first point in the direction of Sepak, if you can indicate and make a circle there, and put -- write the word actually "towards Sepak."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you take this road and go further down some five kilometres onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you mark the direction on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] It's this road indicated by the arrow, downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, I have one more question concerning this map that is in front of you. Yesterday I asked a question, but it wasn't, in my -- I'm not sure if it was clear. Where you have the school circled, you know where I'm talking about where you have a circle around the school. You can see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, just beside, we see a main road that goes towards Dolina. Do you see that main that main road with red and white?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one above the school?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm talking the main road, because there is a -- there is a main intersection. If I say there is the main road that goes from Zvornik Brigade, that's one road; but then there is a T junction and we see there is a road that goes towards Dolina. Now, my question is simply if you can confirm that this main road is not the road that you were in when you were close to the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Main road, it is not; but the junction which leads upwards towards the school 300 to 400 metres, that's where I mean. That's where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We'll see it better in another exhibit I am going to use. That is correct for this exhibit, if you can just sign this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if we can save it again with the new markings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you write the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- as a Defence exhibit, and the date being the 4th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would it be okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's correct with me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Will it be too long or can it be saved? I'm asking the court deputy. That's fine. Thank you. We'll save it as a separate Defence Exhibit and proceed, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived that day in Rocevic, after getting the instructions from your commander, my understanding is when you arrived your fellow military policemen from Z brigade were already present there. You arrived after them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you yourself, throughout your stay there, you never came close to the school itself. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That's the orders we received, because there were other soldiers there providing security. There were just three to four of us who controlled the cars and the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, that's exactly what I wanted to ask about is the other soldiers that you see at the school. Now, you did mention yesterday in your testimony that you did not know these soldiers. What I would like to know is, I believe that as a military policeman, you see many people in Zvornik Brigade. So to you were these soldiers from Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably not, because I would have recognised some of them if they had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, these soldiers that were there, it is also my understanding that it was made clear to you, and I suggest that this is the case, it was made clear to you not to come close to the school, that they were handling the business there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And according to your statements, you left that -- the school towards the end of the afternoon, whether it's 17 or 18, my question is more that the visit that you saw from those security officers. Is it closer to the beginning of your arrival at the school, or closer to the -- to your departure from the school? When did that take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact time, but between that period. Well, it was in between somewhere during that period, but I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So in between, if you arrived around 1.00 and you left, according to your statement, around 6.00, so somewhere around 3.00, would that be correct? Would that be a good reference point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it might have been, but I can't say exactly when the time was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, you and your fellow military policemen, you mentioned in your testimony that there was one colleague with you at some kind of a check-point, and that the others were close to the yard. Do you remember a coffee shop close to the school or close to the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that there was any coffee shop. All I remember is that there was a house there nearby, next to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd like to have on the e-court, please, an exhibit, and this is 3D100.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I will show you the -- a map of the location of the school, and maybe first I should ask you if you recognise this as being a map of the location of the school. So on the e-court before you, you have a sketch, and I'd ask you if you recognise what this sketch represents.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see a sketch of the school and the by-road leading off from the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, just to clarify, a bit earlier I asked you about that main road going to -- let me first ask you. With the assistance of the usher, can you indicate with a circle the general area where you stood that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, this road that we see here where you are, I just want to confirm to you that the other road we see going north, the other road that is to the left of that one going north, that's the main road that you indicated that you were not on, on the other map. Is that correct? Tell me if the question is not clear, because I'm not sure if my question is clear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not clear on what you're asking me, what you mean to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If you look at this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the word "main road" may confuse the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If you look on the map, there are two roads going -- I will see -- there is a road on the left side of the map with an arrow on it going down. Do you see this road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this road here? I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The one with the arrow pointing down at the left of the map. Maybe you can circle that arrow to indicate that you see that road, so that we are on the same road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- I'm just asking you whether this road was the main road that we saw on the map with the colour red and white?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. It wasn't such a sharp bend. It should have been straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll leave it at that, and we will work with this. Now, the house that you mentioned a little earlier as being close to the school, can you circle that house and put simply H, the letter H beside that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So is that the house where your fellow military police stood? Is that the one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said H for school, where the school was, so I put an H and made a circle around it on the road where we were at.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry. Maybe there was a mistake in the word I used. I wanted you to indicate the house where your fellow military policemen were at, the ones that were not at the -- on the road with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, if we could delete the H in the circle. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It's magic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were not in the house. We were outside. Two were on the road, and two were around the yard, checking. We didn't go to any house. There was just a house near us or next to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you indicate which house this is, if you can see it on that sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house was next to us, but it says here a shop. There was no shop open at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you don't see on this sketch the house -- so the house where your fellow military policemen were, I guess, was -- is not indicated on this drawing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on to my next question. Would I be correct in saying that your duties that day, you yourself, that was -- there was no difference in your duties compared to the tasks that were assigned to the other military policemen who were there? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. We received one order from one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you were all doing the same thing; that's my point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we took shifts or turns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, are you done with this sketch?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I would like to keep it there. I will probably use it for something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is whether Madam Usher should be standing there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Well, maybe I will make one more indication, and we can close this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, can you indicate -- make -- is it possible to use another colour of pen? And if we can indicate simply, put an H to the location where that house was, to the best of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But before that, can you clarify, I took it that the witness meant to say that the house was there, but it is expressed as shop now. Could you clarify with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Where it says, "Shop," forget the fact whether it is a shop or not, is it the house that we're talking about or is it another house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After so many years, maybe ten, new houses may have been built in the meantime. At the time it was a shop, and shops open and close.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. So just indicate where the general location of that house, where you stood, was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I will mark it where the shop is now. It wasn't a shop at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a house, with the letter H.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the yard that you described in your testimony earlier, can you just make a big circle around the yard of the school that you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the yard, and the training ground is up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. If you can just indicate the number 165, and then we can close it, and the date also; 4 April 07?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I just ask if my friend knows, because of the question about this diagram and houses and shops, where it's from and if he knows when it was done, what the source is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you clarify, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes. This was done by the authorities, and it was done two weeks ago, on scale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Authorities being?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Municipality authorities that we contacted to get it done two weeks ago or thereabouts, and it was done on scale and it was done using the proper equipment to be on scale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: On scale as it presently is, or were they using records from the time period in question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My understanding is from the existing, today, using equipment today. Does that satisfy my colleague?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. And if you know, municipality authorities, what exactly is -- is this a particular department or do you have any more information on what this is?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I can provide that information later on, if my colleague wants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm surprised the Prosecution didn't do this before, but that's not the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- could you kindly put your name and the date on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Name being your number, actually PW-165. Just 165.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I think we can do away with the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I have one more question just before we go for the break, because I think that will be about time for this. Now, being a military policeman yourself for some time, you have been involved, for sure, in setting up what we call check-points in military police language. What I'd like to know from you is: From your description of the place where you were, was this really a check-point, and what was really going on there in terms of the cars that you were either stopping or not stopping? What exactly was happening there at that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a make-shift check-point. Only two of us were standing on the side. We would stop people by raising our hand. They saw that we were military policemen. We checked people going by.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And some vehicles you would stop more than others, or was it the same procedure for all cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we knew someone, we didn't stop them; but if we didn't know people, we would stop and check them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe it's the right time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a break for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I may begin by calling back the exhibit that I used, the second sketch of the school, just to make a correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which has been marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The one that -- the one which has been marked by the witness. And I guess it's IC85. We had a good laugh over the break and I would like to make that correction because maybe the witness will help us why -- why there was a problem with the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, just quickly, can you tell me if you can tell from where you made that circle and what I called a road, would I be right in saying that this is actually a stream and that the arrow indicates the way the water is flowing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember there being a creek. There's just the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But is that what it says? What is written on that where you made that red circle, what is written there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it. It's illegible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How I remember, Mr. Bourgon, is that the witness was told to circle that arrow, be it a stream or a main road. Told by you to circle the arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Indeed, indeed. That's what the mistake is all about. I thought that was the main road on the map, and I believe it's not. But the witness can't help us with that now, so we'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, let me go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And may we go into closed session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are done with this sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It was just to make a correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thanks for the clarification. And we will go into private session

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Witness, the person I just mentioned when we were in closed session, I'd like to know if you saw that person that day when you were at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I say to you that we have information which was provided to us by the Prosecution that the car normally used by Drago Nikolic was driven that day by Bircakovic, would that help you in -- would that comfort you in the fact that you did not see Drago Nikolic that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question. The witness has testified about what he saw. He can ask him what he saw or what he didn't see. But "comforting" him, I think is an inappropriate way to put the question. And I also frankly don't see why the previous question needed to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think -- could you rephrase the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The fact that -- Witness, the fact that Bircakovic was driving the car normally used by Drago Nikolic, and that you did not see him that day, does that confirm the fact that you did not see Drago Nikolic at Rocevic School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said in my answer, I personally didn't hear -- didn't see him, I only heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: In fact, Witness, the car itself that day, you said that yesterday, but you don't know which car exactly it was, you could not describe the car. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you yourself never looked into the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't have an opportunity to get into this car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you don't know who was driving the car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the answer I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would you remember whether the car had two doors or four doors, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I don't remember the car, I then definitely can't remember how many doors there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I propose to you that you cannot say how many persons were in the car, would that also be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I answered that in response to the previous questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you be -- are you certain about the number of people that were in the car, or is there a doubt in your mind? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see how many people there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, we have information that -- again, coming from the Prosecution, that the person named Bircakovic drove to Rocevic, that school, that this person was not driving Drago Nikolic. Does that confirm that you did not see Drago Nikolic at Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That question is complicated. Could you rephrase it so that the witness can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will try to make the question more simple. The Prosecution has provided us information, according to which Bircakovic drove, not only Drago Nikolic's car that day, but that he was not driving Drago Nikolic that day. Does that confirm that did you not see Drago Nikolic in Rocevic School?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection. That question doesn't make any sense. He's explained that he didn't see this person Bircakovic, that he didn't know necessarily who was driving Drago Nikolic in this time and he didn't see who was in the car. So the question is illogical. The fact that he did not see this person doesn't confirm anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We agree. It is sufficient for the witness to say that he didn't see either Nikolic nor Bircakovic and it is for us to confirm whether he is right or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, were you aware that Bircakovic was driving Drago Nikolic's car that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And were you aware, Witness, that that day Bircakovic was not driving Drago Nikolic around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just answered your question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. Witness, did you know that on that day Drago Nikolic was apparently, according to information we have, on duty at the Zvornik Brigade during the time-frame that you were in Rocevic? Were you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: For the sake of the record and to inform my colleagues, this information is taken from Exhibit P377, the Zvornik Brigade duty officer's logbook; P378, Zvornik Brigade duty officer diary; and thirdly, an expert report which was disclosed to the Defence, a report that dates back to June 2006, notice of which was served on the Defence on the 9th March of 2007. Witness, my next question refers to someone, I would like to know if, is it possible that one of the military policemen who was there with you on that day, that this would be someone called Simic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I now have a few questions concerning your commander, Jasikovac. And you've already said that he was the commander of the military police commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So Jasikovac was the one who was issuing orders to the military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He issued orders to the military police, but he received his orders from his superior.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: confirm that this person was actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Shall we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My friend needs to be a bit -- are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'd just like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- just... Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you one question about the meeting that you were informed or told about when you returned to Zvornik Brigade command. You mentioned that there would have been a meeting with the commander. Can you confirm that someone holding the position of commander was present that night and, if so, who that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it was. I heard that they were coming up there to have a meeting with the commander. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And in your testimony you mentioned the name Obrenovic. Can you confirm that Obrenovic was actually filling in for the commander on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And did you see Obrenovic there that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my previous statement I said that I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, Witness, I have one last question for you. And it's simply that, to your knowledge -- or rather, let me phrase this another way. I propose to you that you yourself, and the military policemen from Zvornik Brigade, were not involved in the killing of Muslims detained in villages close to Zvornik Brigade in July of 1995. Would you agree with this proposition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. I have no further questions. Again, I apologise because you have been here for a long time, 15 days. And with everything that happened, I apologise. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Who is going next? Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Likewise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it will be Mr. Sarapa who will ask questions. Yes, Mr. Sarapa is representing Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: On the day when you came to Rocevic, would you agree with me that you and your colleagues who were there, and when you set up the check-point, your duty was to deny access to the civilians to prisoners of war, practically to protect them from the civilian onslaught?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was our duty, and the entry was being secured by others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: You didn't see these POWs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: In light of that, you apparently don't know how many of them there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Did you know what was to become of them? Could you at least assume what was going to happen to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just an ordinary person, and I couldn't suppose what was about to happen or what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Would you agree with the assertion that if soldiers from the military company -- military police company were not in contact with the POWs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As -- during the time I was there, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes, I was referring to the time you were there. Can you tell me this: When this meeting took place, when you went to the Zvornik Brigade HQ, can we agree that Obrenovic was commanding the brigade, standing in for Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And do you know that Pandurevic was away at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what was the service car that Pandurevic used to use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: At the time did you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Put a pause, yes. Could you ask that question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And put a pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: At the time did you know what car was being used by Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what car he was using.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Very well. For the record, I would like just to make a correction. On page 10, lines 23 and 24, the witness said, when speaking about Obrenovic as the commander who was standing in, the record shows the following:" [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... brigade that was replacing Obrenovic." [Interpretation] In fact it should read that he stood in for Pandurevic. If we can clarify this for the witness, that we are talking about Pandurevic, that Obrenovic stood in for. And in that respect would you agree that at the time the -- the current commander of the brigade was a person standing in for Obrenovic and not Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-165 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer. The interpreters didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that period Obrenovic stood in for Pandurevic, and of course we addressed him as brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now it's clear. Mr. Sarapa, you are done with your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nicholls, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I might, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I was wondering if I could ask for a five to 10-minute break. I'm just looking for a document I might want to put to the witness that has come up through the cross, and I just want to check that. I'm trying to find it, I can't lay my hands on it right now. I'm sorry for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 10 minutes will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
